categories.name: Engine & Fuel System
categories.description: Engine misfires, rough or stalling idle, loss of power, poor acceleration, exhaust smoke, oil leaks or oil pressure warnings, engine belts, and fuel delivery faults.
categories.safety_note: Stop driving immediately if the low oil pressure warning light illuminates, if you smell raw fuel or see a fuel leak, or if severe engine knocking occurs.

categories.name: Starting, Battery & Electrical
categories.description: No-crank or slow cranking on startup, clicking sounds when turning the key, battery warning light, dim or failed headlights, ignition wires, wipers, washer spray, windows, locks, and horn.
categories.safety_note: Turn off the ignition and disconnect the negative battery terminal before probing high-current starter or charging cables, and wear eye protection around lead-acid batteries.

categories.name: Braking & ABS System
categories.description: Soft, spongy, or hard brake pedal, squealing brakes, pedal pulsation, steering vibration under braking, pulling or dragging brakes, brake fluid leaks, and ABS or brake warning lights.
categories.safety_note: CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: Do not drive the vehicle if the brake pedal feels soft/spongy, sinks toward the floor, or if active brake fluid leakage is visible.

categories.name: Cooling & Cabin Heating
categories.description: Engine overheating, temperature gauge in the red zone, coolant leaks under the vehicle, sweet coolant smell in the cabin, no cabin heat, radiator, cooling fan, hoses, and water pump.
categories.safety_note: THERMAL BURN HAZARD: Never open a radiator or pressurized coolant reservoir cap while the engine is hot. Shut off an overheating engine safely and allow it to cool completely.

categories.name: Transmission, Clutch & Drivetrain
categories.description: Slipping gears, delayed or erratic shifting, transmission overheating, shuddering, soft or loose clutch pedal, driveline vibration, clunking, differential whine, and binding on turns.
categories.safety_note: Secure the vehicle on level ground with wheel chocks before inspecting underbody transmission, clutch hydraulic, differential, or axle components.

categories.name: Exhaust & Emissions System
categories.description: Check engine light paired with rough idle, rotten-egg exhaust smell, fuel vapor odor, gas cap warning light, engine knocking/pinging, or loud exhaust manifold leaks.
categories.safety_note: CARBON MONOXIDE HAZARD: Never run an engine in an enclosed garage, and have cabin exhaust odors inspected immediately before driving with windows closed.

categories.name: Air Conditioning & Ventilation
categories.description: No cold air or warm air from AC vents, weak or absent cabin airflow, musty vent odors, loud AC compressor or blower noises, and erratic HVAC fan speeds.
categories.safety_note: AC refrigerant circuits are pressurized; leak repairs and refrigerant handling should be performed with proper recovery equipment.

categories.name: Steering, Wheels & Tires
categories.description: Noise or stiff effort when turning the steering wheel, grinding or clicking noises from wheels, wheel wobbling, highway vibration with uneven tire wear, and TPMS tire-pressure warnings.
categories.safety_note: Do not drive at highway speeds if wheel wobbling, severe wheel grinding, or sudden steering stiffness is present; inspect lug nuts, wheel hubs, and tire inflation safely.

rules.title: ABS Control Module
rules.affected_component: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) Electronic Control Unit & Hydraulic Block

maintenance_actions.corrective_action: Inspect ABS power fuse and relay. Test harness ground and CAN bus continuity. If internal solenoid valve or microprocessor fault is confirmed by scan, replace ABS module and pressure-bleed system.
maintenance_actions.preventive_maintenance: Flush brake fluid every 2 years / 40,000 km to prevent moisture accumulation and solenoid corrosion in the ABS valve body.
maintenance_actions.replacement_criteria: Replace only if scanner confirms internal open/short in module solenoids or power driver circuit, with external wiring verified intact.
maintenance_actions.do_not_replace_warning: Do not replace the ABS module without first checking the ABS power fuse, chassis ground connection, and wheel speed sensor signals.

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the ABS warning light illuminate immediately when the vehicle was turned on, before moving?
diagnostic_questions.context: A fault light at startup before vehicle motion points to power, ground, or module self-test failure rather than a wheel sensor pulse issue.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the brake pedal pulsate or chatter on dry, non-slippery pavement under light braking?
diagnostic_questions.context: Inappropriate ABS activation on dry pavement indicates false wheel speed signals or erratic control module command.

contradictory_evidence: ABS warning light turns off after startup self-test and stays off
Braking is smooth with zero pedal kickback on dry pavement

system_hierarchy.component: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) Electronic Control Unit & Hydraulic Block

rules.rule_expression: IF "ABS warning light is on" AND "Brake pedal pulsation" THEN Possible Fault Candidate = "ABS Control Module"
possible_causes: Blown (check abs fuse)
Faulty wiring (inspect wiring to abs module)
recommended_checks: Step 1: Check ABS fuse — check whether finding is 'Blown' vs. 'Intact'.
Step 2: Inspect wiring to ABS module — check whether finding is 'Faulty wiring' vs. 'Good wiring'.
rules.suggested_next_steps: Perform the 2 diagnostic verification checks in order (Check ABS fuse; Inspect wiring to ABS module). Only service or replace ABS Control Module components if physical inspection confirms 'Blown' or 'Faulty wiring'.
rules.safety_warning: CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: Do not drive the vehicle if the brake pedal feels soft/spongy, sinks toward the floor, or if active brake fluid leakage is visible.

rules.title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor
rules.possible_fault: Possible ABS Wheel Speed Sensor issue
rules.affected_component: Wheel Speed Reluctor Sensor & Tone Ring Assembly

maintenance_actions.corrective_action: Inspect sensor harness for chafing or cut wires. Clean metallic debris from magnetic sensor tip and tone ring teeth. If sensor coil is open or hall sensor output is dead, replace wheel speed sensor.
maintenance_actions.preventive_maintenance: Inspect sensor wiring routing during tire rotations and brake pad replacements.
maintenance_actions.replacement_criteria: Replace if sensor resistance is out of factory specification (typically 800-1400 ohms for passive, or no square-wave pulse on active sensors).
maintenance_actions.do_not_replace_warning: Do not replace the sensor until inspecting the reluctor tone ring for cracked teeth, rust build-up, or excessive air gap.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the ABS light turn on only after the vehicle exceeds 15-20 km/h (10-15 mph)?
diagnostic_questions.context: Wheel speed sensor signal loss faults typically trigger once the vehicle begins rolling and the ECU detects a missing frequency pulse.

contradictory_evidence: ABS light never triggers during driving
All 4 wheel speeds read identically on live scanner data

rules.title: Brake Booster
rules.affected_component: Vacuum Brake Power Booster & Check Valve Assembly
required_tools: Handheld Vacuum Pump with Gauge (0-30 in-Hg)

maintenance_actions.corrective_action: Inspect vacuum supply line from intake manifold for cracks, oil contamination, or collapse. Test one-way check valve operation. If booster diaphragm leaks vacuum internally, replace brake booster unit.
maintenance_actions.preventive_maintenance: Inspect rubber vacuum supply hose for softness, hardening, or engine oil ingress during major services.
maintenance_actions.replacement_criteria: Replace booster if it fails the pedal-drop holding test (pedal does not drop when engine starts, or hisses continuously during application).
maintenance_actions.do_not_replace_warning: Do not replace the brake booster without first confirming engine manifold vacuum supply (at least 16-20 in-Hg at idle) and check valve integrity.

diagnostic_questions.question: When pressing the brake pedal before starting the engine, does the pedal drop down slightly once the engine starts running?
diagnostic_questions.context: Normal brake boosters draw vacuum on engine start, pulling the pedal down slightly; failure to drop indicates vacuum assist loss.

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you hear a continuous hissing sound from underneath the driver dashboard when you press or release the brake pedal?
diagnostic_questions.context: A hissing noise inside the cabin near the pedals indicates a ruptured internal booster rubber diaphragm leaking atmospheric air.

contradictory_evidence: Brake pedal drops smoothly when engine starts
Pedal effort is light and responsive with normal power assist

system_hierarchy.component: Vacuum Brake Power Booster & Check Valve Assembly

Low vacuum pressure (test brake booster vacuum pressure)
recommended_checks: Step 1: Check brake booster vacuum hose — check whether finding is 'Leaking' vs. 'Intact'.
Step 2: Test brake booster vacuum pressure — check whether finding is 'Low vacuum pressure' vs. 'Normal vacuum pressure'.
rules.suggested_next_steps: Perform the 2 diagnostic verification checks in order (Check brake booster vacuum hose; Test brake booster vacuum pressure). Only service or replace Brake Booster components if physical inspection confirms 'Leaking' or 'Low vacuum pressure'.

rules.title: Brake Caliper
rules.affected_component: Hydraulic Disc Brake Caliper & Slider Pins Assembly
required_tools: Brake Line Clamp / Fluid Catch Pan

maintenance_actions.corrective_action: Inspect caliper guide slider pins for corrosion and seize-up. Check piston dust boot for tears and hydraulic leaks. Re-grease slider pins or replace seized caliper assembly, followed by hydraulic system bleeding.
maintenance_actions.preventive_maintenance: Clean and lubricate guide pins with high-temperature silicone ceramic brake grease at every pad replacement.
maintenance_actions.replacement_criteria: Replace caliper if piston is frozen in the bore, piston chrome is pitted, or fluid leaks past the internal square-cut seal.
maintenance_actions.do_not_replace_warning: Do not replace caliper for uneven pad wear until checking if slider pins are simply dry or sticking in their rubber boots.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the vehicle consistently pull to one side when you brake, or does one wheel rim feel noticeably hotter than the others after driving?
diagnostic_questions.context: A seized caliper piston or guide pin keeps brake pads dragging, generating excessive wheel heat and steering pull.

contradictory_evidence: Vehicle stops straight with hands lightly touching wheel
All wheel hubs remain at identical moderate temperature after driving

rules.title: Brake Hose
rules.affected_component: Flexible Hydraulic Reinforced Brake Hose

maintenance_actions.corrective_action: Inspect rubber exterior for cracking, chafing, blistering, or fluid seepage under pressure. If internal hose layer collapses (acting as a one-way check valve) or leaks externally, replace flexible hose immediately.
maintenance_actions.preventive_maintenance: Replace flexible rubber brake hoses every 6-8 years or whenever deep weather-checking cracks appear.
maintenance_actions.replacement_criteria: Replace immediately if any external bulge, wetness, or deep cracking is visible.
maintenance_actions.do_not_replace_warning: Always use a flare-nut wrench on hydraulic fittings to prevent rounding soft steel brake line nuts.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does an assistant notice any ballooning or expansion along the flexible rubber brake hose when the pedal is pressed hard?
diagnostic_questions.context: Internal cord failure causes hydraulic pressure to balloon the hose outward instead of clamping the brake pads.
